The width chain that starves the mini-cards. `.body { display:grid; grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr; gap: var(--space-lg); align-items:start; }` (39-44) — the job queue sits in the 1fr column. `.collapsibleCard` adds `border: 1px solid var(--border)`; `.collapsibleBody { padding: 0 var(--space-md) var(--space-md); }` (82-84) removes another 32px. `.inner { width:100%; max-width:1120px; min-width:0; }` — 1120 > 1006, so it is not the binding constraint at 1280px; the content column is the full 1006px.
`.page { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap: var(--space-md); }` — no horizontal padding, so it does not narrow the column further.

`export function TextInput(props: InputHTMLAttributes<HTMLInputElement>)` — a bare passthrough: `<input className={[styles.input, className].filter(Boolean).join(" ")} {...rest} />`. Every extra attribute the lane adds (e.g. `autoCorrect`, `spellCheck`, `data-*`) forwards to the real <input> with no allowlist. `className` is MERGED, not replaced, so `.input`'s base rules always apply.

The base input recipe the PIN field inherits, including the focus ring: `.input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-accent); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--color-focus); animation: loombre-input-focus-in var(--motion-fast) var(--ease-spring); }` (lines 48-52). The 21-line comment at 27-47 explains the ring is INSET specifically because SheetOrModal.module.css `.body { overflow-y: auto; }` clips a non-inset ring. Critically: an INSET ring on a 1px x 1px visually-hidden box renders nothing visible — this is exactly why LD-17 requires the ring be moved to the dots container.

`.body { min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; }` — the clipping ancestor that forced Input.module.css's inset ring. Focus trap / scroll lock / Escape. FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR includes `input:not([disabled])`, and getFocusableElements deliberately does NOT filter on offsetParent/offsetWidth (documented at 30-37), so a visually-hidden 1x1 input REMAINS in the trap's tab cycle — LD-17's 'focusable' requirement is compatible with the existing trap with no changes needed there. useFocusTrap's Tab handler is a CAPTURE-phase document keydown listener (line 89) but it early-returns on anything that is not `Tab` (line 67), so it never intercepts digit keys. useEscapeKey (126-135) only handles 'Escape'. The pure buffer logic both input paths route through. `sanitizePinInput` = strip non-digits then `.slice(0, 4)`. `appendPinDigit` is a no-op once the buffer is full. `isPinComplete(pin)` is `pin.length === 4` — the auto-submit trigger.

THE existing precedent for both halves of LD-17 — see `existingVisuallyHiddenUtil` below for the verbatim rule. Line 63-65 is the sibling focus-ring transfer: `.input:focus-visible + .track { box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus-ring); }`. In PinModal the dots PRECEDE the input (PinModal.tsx:100-104 then 112-123), so `+`/`~` cannot reach backwards — the lane needs `.form:has(input.hiddenInput:focus-visible) .dots { … }` (or an equivalent), and `:has()` is currently used NOWHERE in apps/web's CSS (grep: zero hits across all *.css).

pinDialog.focusHandling:
INITIAL FOCUS — two mechanisms compete, and the trap almost certainly wins:
  (a) `autoFocus` on the TextInput (PinModal.tsx:117). React applies autoFocus during the commit/layout phase.
  (b) `useFocusTrap(dialogRef, open)` (SheetOrModal.tsx:53) runs a passive `useEffect` (overlay-hooks.ts:55-95) whose mount body does `const focusables = getFocusableElements(container); (focusables[0] ?? container).focus();` (lines 62-63). Passive effects run AFTER the commit phase, and a parent's effect runs after its children's, so this fires last.
In DesktopDialog's DOM order the first focusable is the header's ghost 'Done' <Button> (SheetOrModal.tsx:73-75, a real <button> per Button.tsx:20), which precedes `.body`. So on open, focus lands on 'Done', not the PIN input — meaning the existing `autoFocus` is very likely already dead. FLAGGED FOR LIVE VERIFICATION: Phase 0 is read-only and this was not executed. If confirmed, LD-17's 'hardware-keyboard entry must keep working' requires an explicit focus move to the input on open, not merely preserving `autoFocus`.

FOCUS TRAP: overlay-hooks.ts:66-87 installs a CAPTURE-phase `document` keydown listener that early-returns on anything that is not `Tab` (line 67), then cycles Tab/Shift+Tab between first and last focusable. `getFocusableElements` (29-38) deliberately does NOT filter by visibility, so a visually-hidden input STAYS in the cycle — LD-17's 'focusable' requirement needs no change to the trap.

FOCUS RETURN: overlay-hooks.ts:58 records `document.activeElement` on open; the cleanup at 92-93 restores it on close.

WHERE THE RING SHOWS TODAY: on the input itself, from Input.module.css:48-52 — `.input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-accent); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--color-focus); animation: loombre-input-focus-in ...; }`. It is INSET on purpose (21-line rationale at Input.module.css:27-47: SheetOrModal.module.css `.body { overflow-y: auto; }` clips a non-inset ring, and the global keyframe at globals.css:82-90 would otherwise re-clobber it back to non-inset). CONSEQUENCE FOR LD-17: an inset ring on a 1x1 clipped box paints nothing at all, so the ring MUST move to `.dots` — the existing per-element ring cannot simply be inherited.

RING TRANSFER — the structural problem the lane must solve: the codebase's precedent is Toggle.module.css:63-65, `.input:focus-visible + .track { box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus-ring); }`, which works because Toggle's hidden input PRECEDES the painted element. In PinModal the ORDER IS REVERSED — `.dots` at PinModal.tsx:100-104, then the input at 112-123 — so `+` and `~` cannot reach backwards, and LD-17 fixes the input's position ('between the dots and the keypad'), so reordering is not available. The workable route is `:has()`, e.g. `.form:has(input.hiddenInput:focus-visible) .dots { box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus-ring); }`. `:has()` appears in ZERO CSS files in apps/web today (grep across all *.css: no hits), so this would be its first use; nothing in apps/web/.stylelintrc.json forbids it (the only value restriction is `declaration-property-value-allowed-list` on border-radius, which allows only `var(--radius-*)` literals — relevant if the lane adds a radius to a ring on `.dots`, which is currently `display:flex; gap: var(--space-sm);` with no radius of its own).

OTHER FOCUS SURFACES IN THE DIALOG: the 11 keypad buttons get `.key:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--shadow-focus-ring); }` (PinModal.module.css:120-123) — a NON-inset ring, already shipping inside SheetOrModal's clipping `.body` without a reported problem, which is useful evidence that a non-inset ring on `.dots` will also survive that clip.

CLICK HANDLERS: there is NO click handler anywhere that focuses the input — clicking a dot does nothing, and clicking a keypad button moves focus to that button (native), taking focus AWAY from the input. Once the input is visually hidden this is a real trap: after any keypad press, subsequent hardware-keyboard digits will no longer reach the input (see hardwareKeyboardPath). No `onMouseDown`/`preventDefault` guard exists on the keys today.
pinDialog.hardwareKeyboardPath:
Hardware-keyboard digits reach the value through EXACTLY ONE path: the `<TextInput>`'s own `onChange` (PinModal.tsx:121):

          onChange={(e) => setPin(sanitizePinInput(e.target.value))}

That is a controlled React input (`value={pin}`, line 119) with `maxLength={PIN_LENGTH}` (118). A typed character produces a native input event -> React onChange -> `sanitizePinInput` (lib/pin-entry.ts:29-31, strip non-digits + slice(0,4)) -> `setPin` -> the auto-submit effect (54-61) runs when length hits 4.

There is NO document-level, form-level, or dialog-level keydown/keypress listener that captures digits anywhere in this path. Verified:
  - PinModal.tsx has one keyboard handler, `handleKeypadKeyDown` (81-91), and it is bound only to the nine digit BUTTONS, only fires on Enter/Space, and does nothing with digit keys.
  - components/restricted/RestrictedProvider.tsx contains no addEventListener/keydown at all (grep).
  - overlay-hooks.ts's two document listeners are `useFocusTrap`'s capture-phase keydown, which early-returns on anything that is not 'Tab' (overlay-hooks.ts:67), and `useEscapeKey`'s, which only handles 'Escape' (129-131).
  - `<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>` (PinModal.tsx:95) only calls `event.preventDefault()` (65-69) so Enter in the field never reloads the page.

THEREFORE: hardware-keyboard entry works if and only if the visually-hidden input HOLDS FOCUS. Two live hazards the lane must handle, both consequences of hiding the input rather than of LD-17's wording:
  (1) On open, the focus trap appears to move focus to the header's 'Done' button rather than the input (see focusHandling) — so the input may not be focused to begin with. Today a sighted desktop user can just click the visible 160px field; once it is 1x1 and clipped, there is nothing to click.
  (2) Any keypad button press moves focus to that <button> (native behavior; no preventDefault on mousedown anywhere), so a mixed interaction — tap '1' on the keypad, then type '2','3','4' — silently stops working. Today that is masked because the visible field can be clicked back into.
A robust implementation needs the dots/form to route focus back to the input (e.g. an onMouseDown preventDefault on the keys, or an explicit inputRef.focus() after each keypad press), and to focus the input on open. Neither exists today; there is no ref on the input at all (PinModal.tsx:43 declares only `submittingRef`, used for the auto-submit guard).

PASTE also works today through the same onChange (a 4-digit paste sanitizes and auto-submits) and will continue to, since paste targets the focused input.
